conviction_note: Nothing has been pre-released, so the Q3 numbers are new. The 2026 guide is two fixed numbers (4,000 MSEK revenue, 3.9% adj. EBITA margin, from the 2026-05-26 CMD). Revenue is tracking above it and the margin needs a big H2 step-up, so the move sits on the guide line, scaled at 7% for a thin single-analyst name. Every finding is a proxy, a comparison base or an arithmetic inference rather than an unseen company number, so p_up is held at 54. The findings sum to +1.1 against a scaled +0.56; they are sized one by one, and the gap is p_up held near 50 because the Q3-2025 margin miss drew -10.1%.

new_in_release.expect: Q3 revenue and adj. EBITA, not pre-released. Expect strong YoY growth on an easy base (Q3-25 adj. EBITA 20.7 MSEK, 2.6% margin, hit by Denmark and Norvia). Roughly in line to slightly above the implied bar.

Revenue guide of 4,000 MSEK: a raise or 'above' wording is plausible (H1 +23%, single-analyst consensus 4.11bn). The 3.9% margin guide is the risk line, because it needs an H2 margin of about 5% against 3.4% in H2-25. Most likely outcome is reiterated or revenue-only raised; the sign of any change is uncertain.
Status of the Finnish claims on older state contracts. Unknown; any resolution would be a one-off.
Q3 is seasonally weak for cash. Peer Svevia had positive operating cash flow in Q3. Unknown for Terranor.
Order backlog (7.3bn at Q2). Q3-Q4 wins are public, so a modest rise is expected and largely priced.

findings.finding: Svevia, Sweden's state-owned road-maintenance peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-22. Its Drift (road O&M) division had the group's largest order-intake increase, from higher volumes within existing contracts, and slightly higher operating profit, which supports Terranor's Swedish extra-works driver. The same report flags asphalt prices raised by high energy prices, a cost risk for Terranor's Finnish state contracts, which have high material-cost ratios and ceiling-price mechanisms (company FY2025 report). Net slightly positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-11) fell -10.1% when adj. EBITA dropped to 20.7 (28.8) on a Denmark shortfall. FY25 (2026-02-17) -1.8%, Q1-26 (2026-05-12) 0.0%, Q2-26 (2026-08-25) +2.6%, all close-to-close from Yahoo.
findings.original_quote: "Störst ökning återfanns inom division Drift till följd av ökade volymer i befintliga kontrakt." (The largest increase [in order intake] was in the Drift division, due to increased volumes in existing contracts.) / "Division Drift redovisade ett något högre rörelseresultat jämfört med föregående år." (Drift reported slightly higher operating profit than last year.) / "Kriget i Mellanöstern har bidragit till fortsatt höga energipriser, vilket har medfört ökade priser för asfalt." (The war in the Middle East has kept energy prices high, which has raised asphalt prices.)
findings.why_not_priced: Svevia is unlisted and publishes in Swedish only, as a PDF on its own site. No English wire or Terranor coverage picked it up. Terranor's tape since 2026-10-22 is flat (36-38 SEK on 20-75k shares a day), with no reaction a peer read-across would leave. The one analyst has used Svevia before (Carnegie note 2026-02-04), so it is partly priced at most.

The asphalt-cost leg is backed by Terranor's FY2025 report on Finnish ceiling-price contracts: https://mfn.se/cis/a/terranor-group/terranor-group-ab-year-end-report-january-december-2025-59b235b1

findings.finding: The Q3 2025 base is depressed: adj. EBITA 20.7 MSEK (2.6% margin) against 28.8 a year earlier, attributed to Denmark's closing-out of state contracts and the Norvia/Infra restructuring. Norvia/Infra were restructured 'with full effect from January 2026', and the four new Danish state contracts 'developed according to plan' in Q2. That points to a large YoY adj. EBITA increase in Q3 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line drew -10.1% on 2025-11-11 when it missed. It drew +2.6% on 2026-08-25 when Q2 adj. EBITA rose 61%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The comparison base is public and the single-analyst EPS of 5.03 already implies a steep H2. It is kept small because the comp is easy whatever the bar, and a thin name with one analyst can still be surprised by the size of the swing.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 report on Denmark and Sweden developing to plan: https://mfn.se/cis/a/terranor-group/interim-report-january-june-2026-1789987f

findings.finding: Guidance arithmetic: H1 revenue of 1,946 MSEK means the 4,000 MSEK guide needs H2 growth of only about 2% YoY (H2-25 2,017.6), after H1 grew 23%. A revenue raise is therefore plausible, and the single analyst already sits at 4.11bn. But the 3.9% margin guide implies about 156 MSEK of adj. EBITA, so H2 needs about 109 MSEK against 68.9 in H2-25 (+58%, roughly a 5% H2 margin against 3.4%). The release is where that gets tested.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-05-26 CMD, where the guide was first given, closed +4.0%, and the stock ran from 28.5 to about 39 by August. There is no prior guide change to measure.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether the release changes the guide is unknown, and the arithmetic cuts both ways (revenue up, margin at risk). Affärsvärlden noted the margin step-up in June. The price (about 37 SEK, roughly 7x the consensus EPS of 5.03) reflects belief in the guide. A cut would be a surprise, and a revenue raise is roughly in consensus already. Management said in August it expects continued profitability improvement in H2 (Quartr summary).
findings.independence: Simply Wall St consensus, 2026-08-28: revenue 4.11bn, EPS 5.03, target 42.50: https://www.webull.ca/news-detail/15478494458102784. Quartr's Q2 summary on H2 confidence: https://quartr.com/events/terranor-group-ternor-q2-2026_FVBVHRbt

findings.finding: On 2026-11-09, the day before the print, about 440k shares (roughly 2% of the ~20m share count, 7-20x normal daily volume) traded in 75k-100k blocks. The price was held at 37.00 and a final 100k print at 37.65 put the stock up about 3% on the day. That reads as institutional demand absorbing size ahead of the print. Insiders are in the MAR closed period, so these are not insider trades.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable. Volume spikes before the prior prints (e.g. 2026-08-21, 143k shares) preceded a +2.6% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly in the price by construction: the price rose to 37.65, which raises the window's base. Who was on the other side, and whether the buyer is done, is not visible. It is kept small because a block has a seller as well as a buyer.

baseline_tension: There is little tension. The lean (+0.08) and the run-up (-1.6% over 20 days, +0.8% over 5 days) are near zero, the findings lean mildly positive, and the anchor is a truncated zero, so there is nothing to beat or agree with.
language_note: Svevia's Q3 2026 interim report is published in Swedish only, as a PDF on svevia.se. It carried the peer read-across that no English source did: Drift order intake up on higher volumes in existing contracts, higher asphalt prices from energy costs, and late-season customer restraint.
Terranor's own releases go out in Swedish and English at once, so the filings added nothing in Swedish that the English versions did not carry.
Swedish press (Affärsvärlden/Placera, June 2026) carried the observation that the 3.9% margin guide needs a much stronger H2. It is the only local commentary found, and it is stale.
lessons_applied: 'Two findings resting on one document are one finding': merged the Svevia volume (+0.8) and Svevia asphalt-cost (-0.6) findings into one at +0.2.

'The move is in the guide' (guidance change, median 9%): merged the revenue-raise (+0.7) and margin-risk (-0.5) findings into one guidance finding at +0.4 with a +/-4 range, and raised abs_move_pct from 6.0 to 7.0.
'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0' / priced comps: cut the easy-comp finding from +0.5 to +0.3, because the base and the consensus EPS are public.
Block-trade positioning finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2: a block has two sides and the price already moved.
'Reaction history vetoes the direction, not the size': p_up kept at 54 rather than raised, because of the -10.1% on the Q3-25 margin miss.
